response.sql: SELECT invoice_number, COUNT(*) AS transaction_count FROM Financial_Transactions WHERE invoice_number IS NOT NULL GROUP BY invoice_number HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN transaction_type <> 'Payment' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 ORDER BY transaction_count DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: An invoice qualifies if it has at least one transaction whose type is not exactly 'Payment'. The case-sensitive comparison uses the default collation, so the SQL does not force case sensitivity. NULL transaction_type is impossible because the column is NOT NULL.
The count shown is all transactions recorded for the invoice, including its 'Payment' transactions, because the request says 'total number of transactions recorded for it'.
Ties in the count are broken arbitrarily, since the request gives no tie-breaker.

alternatives.interpretation: Count only the non-'Payment' transactions per invoice, not all of them.
alternatives.sql: SELECT invoice_number, COUNT(*) AS transaction_count FROM Financial_Transactions WHERE invoice_number IS NOT NULL AND transaction_type <> 'Payment' GROUP BY invoice_number ORDER BY transaction_count DESC LIMIT 10;
